A weak line of convergence associated with a broad trough centered
near Palau and easterly trade winds is sitting over the Marianas and
bringing scattered showers to Guam tonight with isolated 
thunderstorms for all islands. The risk for isolated thunderstorms 
will continue through Monday morning for Guam as an upper-level 
trough moves into the region and wind shear increases significantly. 
However, a diffusive low-level flow and dry upper-level air will 
likely keep storm coverage isolated. By Monday, the upper-level 
trough will start to move out and only isolated showers are 
anticipated until Friday night. As winds decrease over the next 
couple of days, the one exception may be for scattered island-effect
showers in the afternoon over Guam Tuesday and Wednesday. Current 
Tropical Storm In-Fa is expected to make it's closest point of 
approach sometime Friday or Saturday which will bring scattered 
showers for the CNMI and potentially breezy conditions. This 
situation remains highly uncertain, though most models show a passage
through the remote, far northern CNMI with minimal impacts to the 
Marianas. This will continue to be monitored closely for any 
potential changes. See the "Tropical Systems" section for more 
details.

Marine...
Gentle to moderate easterlies will prevail across the Marianas
through Monday, then begin to lighten Monday night especially over
Guam Coastal Waters. A trade-wind convergence zone will continue to 
bring scattered showers tonight. Isolated thunderstorms will also be 
possible through early Monday due to increased upper-level 
instability. Therefore, there is a moderate risk of lightning along 
the coastlines. Combined seas of 6 feet tonight may decrease slightly
with a diminishing west swell but will otherwise persist with the 
dominant east swell through Thursday. This is contributing to a 
moderate risk of rip currents along west-, north-, and east- facing 
reefs. By Friday, seas may increase significantly ahead of current 
Tropical Storm In-Fa that is anticipated to pass somewhere through 
the remote, far northern CNMI islands.

Tropical Systems...
Tropical Storm In-fa is beginning to exit the northern Marshall 
Islands, currently centered near 11.8N 165.1E, or about 190 miles 
east of Enewetak Atoll, 280 miles northwest of Kwajalein Atoll, and
1370 miles east of Guam. Himawari visible satellite shows an area of
deep convection organized about the center, covering Enewetak and
Bikini Atolls, with patchy, discontinuous outer rainbands seen 
within the westerly inflow to its south and southwest, extending 
across Pohnpei. Convective bands extend into the northeast portion of
the storm as well, but the inflow is somewhat cut off by the 
presence of a weaker circulation seen near the Date Line. In-fa is 
forecast to move northwest through Monday with a forward speed 
around 6 or 7 mph, slowing down Monday night through Tuesday as its 
track shifts toward the west-northwest and it continues to intensify.
In-fa's maximum sustained winds are currently at 65 mph, and it may 
strengthen to become a Category 1 typhoon as early as this evening. 
By mid-week, In-fa looks to steadily continue west-northwest as it 
moves between Enewetak in the northern RMI and Wake Island far to the
north, generally moving toward the far northern CNMI through the end
of the week.

For more information on Tropical Storm In-fa, please refer to 
bulletins from the Joint Typhoon Warning Center under WMO header 
WTPN31 PGTW and from the National Weather Service under WMO header 
WTPQ31 PGUM.

Eastern Micronesia...
Tropical Storm In-fa continues to dominate the weather pattern across
the region, even as it begins to exit the northern Marshalls this
afternoon. Scattered showers and isolated thunderstorms persist near
Pohnpei, within the convergent westerly flow south of the storm, but
drier ridging conditions prevail for Kosrae and Majuro, even farther
to the south and southeast. Showers will gradually diminish for
Pohnpei through Tuesday, increasing once more for Pohnpei and Kosrae 
Wednesday and Thursday as In-fa shifts west-northwest, and southwest 
inflow strengthens south of the storm as it begins to pass north of
the region. Majuro can expect a quiet, drier pattern to continue for
much of the coming week.

A Special Weather Statement remains in effect, with the latest 
issuance this afternoon highlighting ongoing hazards across the 
northernmost islands and atolls of the Marshall Islands, as In-fa 
pulls away. However, fairly benign marine conditions continue for the
rest of the region, with combined seas of 4 to 7 feet, comprised 
mainly of primary north to northeast swell and secondary southeast 
swell for Pohnpei and Kosrae, and a primary westerly swell and 
secondary northeast swell for Majuro. West to southwest swell looks
